text:
Dear Dr. Montgomery,

Thank you for evaluating Chloe Reynolds, a 16-year-old student athlete who was referred following routine sports clearance screening. She notes feeling somewhat fatigued after cross-country running, but otherwise feels well. She takes a daily multivitamin and no prescription medications. Her family history is non-contributory, and both parents are in good health.

Her vital signs are normal, with a blood pressure of 114/72 mmHg and a resting heart rate of 68 bpm. Physical examination is generally unremarkable: cardiopulmonary auscultation is normal, and her abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without palpable organomegaly. She does, however, have slight scleral icterus.

Her initial laboratory investigation revealed a reduced hemoglobin of 9.4 g/dL, reflecting an ongoing process of hemolysis-driven anemia. The mean cell volume was low at 72 fL. There was a vigorous marrow response, with her reticulocyte counts showing a marked elevation at 7.6%. On review of the peripheral blood smear, there were abundant dense, small spherical red cells lacking central pallor. Chemistry profiling showed that the total fraction of bilirubin was raised at 3.8 mg/dL, predominantly unconjugated. Further laboratory evaluation demonstrated heightened red cell breakdown during hypotonic exposure, confirming an abnormal elevation in erythrocyte osmotic fragility.

I would appreciate your expert hematologic assessment regarding these findings and your recommendations for further diagnostic evaluation and ongoing care.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Vance
